 ANALYSIS:

 Zoning Code Amendment

 The City of South Gate’s General Plan goals and policies aim to foster vibrant, diverse, and
 sustainable community spaces that encourage economic development and enhance the quality of
 life for residents and visitors alike. The Open Space (OS) zoning district is designated for areas
 that are primarily dedicated to parks, recreational facilities, and natural areas, with the intent to
 preserve open land and provide public recreational opportunities. Integrating compatible and
 complementary uses such as dining and restaurant services within certain Open Space areas can
 enhance the public's experience of parks and open spaces, while supporting local businesses and
 promoting economic development. The addition of dine-in restaurants with ancillary alcohol sales
 in select Open Space areas can provide greater amenities for visitors, encourage longer visits, and
 create a welcoming atmosphere for families, tourists, and local residents to enjoy public spaces.
 The presence of restaurants with ancillary alcohol sales in designated Open Space areas can create
 opportunities for local businesses to thrive, attracting new customers, and boosting the local
 economy.

 The City of South Gate Zoning Ordinance is part of the SGMC (Title 11, Zoning) and contains
 multiple sections describing the different zones within the City, general definitions as commonly
 used within the Title, entitlement processes, procedures for amendments to the Zoning Ordinance
 and regulations regarding land use, property development regulations, signs and parking. The land
 use permission tables in Chapter 11.21 of the Zoning Code establish the uses to which land in each
 zone may be put. Within this chapter, Table 11.21-5 specifies the types of land uses allowed in the
 OS zone. Under this table, dine-in restaurants and related alcohol sales currently are not listed as
 permitted uses in the OS zone; therefore, are prohibited within public and private parks,
 community recreation facilities, and open space resources throughout the city.

 Table 11.21-5 of the City’s Zoning Code is proposed to be amended to permit dine-in restaurants
 and related ancillary alcohol sales as an accessory use in the Open Space (OS) zone, subject to the

Business Operations

The Sofive Soccer Complex was established in South Gate Park in 2019 and has been operating
under a Ground Lease Agreement with the City. The business currently operates Monday through
Friday from 2:00pm to 11:00pm, and Saturday and Sunday from 8:00am to 11:00pm. The facility
is staffed with a total of 30 employees. Its onsite café is equipped with a complete kitchen facility;
however, currently offers a menu of concession-style items such as nachos, fries, chicken tenders,
water, and sports drinks. The project seeks to obtain approval to allow the sale of beer and wine
for on-site consumption in conjunction with the café/restaurant. As part of the request, the
applicant proposes to operate as a traditional restaurant by incorporating a variety of appetizers,
entree meals, and desserts (Attachment 5) to its menu and offering traditional dining services to
patrons. Alcoholic beverages are proposed to be served at all times during the business hours of
operation, and consumption will only be permitted in designated portions of the clubhouse. A
recommended condition of approval will require the applicant to stop selling alcohol at 10:30pm,
which is one-half-hour before closing time. The proposed designated areas for consumption of
beer and wine encompasses the restaurant dining area (810 square feet), a lounge (589 square feet),
party room (298 square feet), diner/café (120 square feet), and outdoor patio space (1,011 square
feet). Consumption of alcohol will be prohibited adjacent to or on the soccer fields. To ensure that
alcohol drinks are only consumed within the restaurant, staff recommends a condition of approval
prohibiting alcoholic drinks outside of the restaurant, except for the outdoor patio area that is
designated for dining. Should an approval be granted, the applicant proposes to hire up to seven
(7) full-time employees including bartenders, cooks, and security personnel. The business will
operate with eight (8) to ten (10) employees per shift.

The current seating configuration comprises a mix of fixed and non-fixed chairs, tables, and stools
for a total of 60 persons. The applicant proposes to increase the current seating capacity to a new
total of 88 persons. The proposed seating layout will include communal-style tables throughout
restaurant/café, with each table having a capacity for eight (8) persons. Three (3) tables will be
located in the restaurant dining area, three (3) tables will be located in the lounge, one (1) table is
proposed within the party room, and four (4) tables within the outdoor patio area.

Pursuant to SGMC Chapter 11.60 (Definitions), a “restaurant” is defined as, “…Any establishment
operated for the primary purpose of providing food, beverages, or meals for compensation that has
suitable kitchen facilities for the preparation, storage, and service of food… Any bar area with all
applicable licenses is typically limited to approximately five hundred square feet or approximately
thirty percent of the dining area; bar areas exceeding these limits are classified as a bar.” Although,
“bars” and “lounges” are not defined within the Zoning Code, they are associated with each other
due to their similar operating characteristics. Therefore, should approval of a CUP be granted, staff

CUP Analysis

As noted above, restaurants and alcohol sales are currently prohibited within the OS zone.
However, if the City Council adopts the proposed Ordinance, restaurants with ancillary alcohol
sales will become permitted uses subject to the approval of a Conditional Use Permit. Therefore,
the applicant’s request for approval of a CUP is contingent upon the adoption of the proposed
Ordinance.

In granting approval of a CUP, the Planning Commission (or the City Council on appeal) shall
make all of the following findings, as applicable to the property:

A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of
  this title or the City’s General Plan in that the City's General Plan emphasizes promoting
  quality recreational opportunities, enhancing community amenities, and supporting
  sustainable and balanced development. Allowing a dine-in restaurant/café with alcohol
  sales within the Sofive Soccer Complex supports these goals by providing a social and
  recreational venue that encourages longer visitation, community engagement, and
  opportunities for social gathering. The proposed use will not undermine any goals related
  to open space preservation or public health, as it is specifically tied to an active recreational
  use (the soccer complex) and will be subject to appropriate controls under the CUP,
  including conditions regarding the sale and consumption of alcohol. The proposed use
  aligns with the General Plan’s policies for improving public amenities and enhancing the
  visitor experience in active recreational areas.

  The Open Space (OS) zoning district is intended to preserve and enhance open space areas
  for recreation, passive uses, and other public activities. The proposed use of a dine-in
  restaurant with alcohol sales complements the recreational and community-oriented nature
  of the existing Sofive Soccer Complex. As an existing, established sports complex, the
  proposed restaurant/café will provide a food and beverage option that enhances the overall
  experience for visitors to the site. The addition of alcohol sales (beer and wine) in
  conjunction with this existing use does not conflict with the primary intent of the OS zone,
  which encourages activities that foster public enjoyment and leisure. Furthermore, the
  request to allow alcohol sales as part of the restaurant operation is designed to be a
  controlled, low-impact use that will not interfere with or negatively affect surrounding open
  space uses.

B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with
  the existing and future land uses of the applicable zone in that a restaurant/café with ancillary
  alcohol sales will be located within the existing Sofive soccer complex, which is an active
  recreational facility that serves the surrounding community. This use is entirely consistent
  with the current purpose of the Open Space (OS) zone, which is to provide space for
  recreational, community-serving, and public activities. The existing soccer complex is
  already a destination for social and recreational activities, and the addition of a restaurant
  with alcohol service is an enhancement that will directly support and complement these
  existing uses. The design of the restaurant and its integration with the soccer complex

  The Open Space (OS) zone is typically intended to preserve areas for parks, recreational

  restaurant/café and alcohol sales are consistent with this long-term vision, as they serve to
  enrich the visitor experience and provide an amenity for users of the facility. The
  introduction of food and beverage services, including alcohol, is compatible with the types
  of recreational uses envisioned for the OS zoning district. As such, the proposed development

  it will not hinder the future uses or long-term development of the zone.

  The location of the restaurant/café within the Sofive Soccer Complex will be sensitive to the
  open space environment. No site improvements or changes to the physical character of the
  complex are proposed, and the existing landscaping, parking, and recreational areas will
  remain intact. This ensures that the open space and recreational qualities of the site are
  preserved while providing a complementary service to those using the complex. The project
  does not alter the fundamental purpose or aesthetic of the OS zoning district but instead
  enhances it by providing a social space for visitors.

C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the
  character or function of the neighborhood in that the proposed use is located within the
  established Sofive soccer complex, which already serves as a community-oriented
  recreational facility. This facility is designed to accommodate high levels of activity and
  visitor traffic, including sports events, social gatherings, and community functions. The
  addition of a restaurant/café with alcohol sales will not significantly alter the nature of the
  existing use, but rather will enhance the visitor experience in a way that is consistent with
  the recreational atmosphere. As the property is already a hub of activity, the proposed land
  use is compatible with the existing character and function of the site and will not introduce
  any uses that are out of character with the surrounding recreational environment.

  The recommended conditions of approval will ensure that the sale and consumption of
  alcohol is done responsibly and does not negatively impact the surrounding residential,
  school, and church uses. These conditions include limits on the hours of alcohol service to
  align with family-friendly and community-oriented activities at the soccer complex, and to
  minimize conflicts with adjacent sensitive uses. Specifically, the restaurant will be required
  to cease alcohol sales at least one-half-hour prior to closing, ensuring that alcohol-related
  activity does not extend beyond the business hours. These conditions are designed to
  minimize any potential for noise, loitering, or disruptive behavior. Another condition of
  approval will prohibit the consumption of alcohol on the soccer fields or adjacent areas.
  This restriction ensures that alcohol consumption is confined to the designated
  restaurant/café area and will not spill over into the recreational fields or surrounding open
  space. By limiting alcohol consumption to a controlled and supervised environment, the
  CUP ensures that the primary use of the fields for sports and family-friendly activities
  remains unaffected. This mitigates any concerns regarding disruptive behavior or alcohol-

the SGMC, and all the required findings in support of a CUP will be made.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS:

The Planning Commission’s act of recommending adoption of the Zoning Code Amendment is
not subject to CEQA review because it is not an “approval” of the Zoning Code Amendment, as
defined in CEQA Guidelines Section 15352, but is rather a recommendation of approval, and
therefore does not commit the City to any definite course of action regarding the Zoning Code
Amendment.

Furthermore, in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project
(request for approval of a CUP) qualifies for a categorical exemption under CEQA Guidelines
Section 15301, (Class 1) “Existing Facilities”, in that the project will not result in any alterations
or expansion to the existing buildings within the project site.

COMMENTS FROM OTHER DEPARTMENTS:

Staff routed the project for comments to several City Departments including the Public Works,
Parks and Recreation, Police Department, Code Enforcement, and the Building & Safety Division.
If the project is approved, the comments received from the departments would be incorporated as

Dear Sirs and Madams:

  We are pleased to announce that our office has been engaged by Sofive Soccer Center-
South Gate (“Sofive”) to process a Conditional Use Permit Application for the premise located at
9599 Pinehurst Avenue, South Gate, CA 90280. The request is to permit or otherwise allow the
issuance of a California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (“ABC”) Type 41 On-Sale
Beer & Wine – Eating Place liquor license, as described more fully herein.

  REQUEST

  Applicant is in the process of filing an application with the California Department of
Alcoholic Beverage Control for an On-Sale Beer & Wine – Eating Place Type 41 license to expand
its current café to include ancillary beer and wine selections for on-site consumption. This license
allows the Applicant to sell beer and wine for consumption on the premises where sold. Distilled
spirits may not be on the premises. The Applicant must operate and maintain the licensed premises
as a bona fide eating place. The Applicant must maintain suitable kitchen facilities and must make
actual and substantial sales of meals for consumption on the premises. This project will utilize the
existing restaurant café to expand its sales to patrons to include ancillary beer and wine selections
for on-site consumption in the limited area depicted in the enclosed materials included herein.

  BACKGROUND

  Principals of Sofive Charles Lagayette and Jean-Damien Ladeuil met over a decade ago at
business school in Paris. The two bonded over soccer and found it difficult to find places to play
their beloved sport when they moved to New York, as many soccer clubs in America didn’t have
dedicated venues for teams to play. Filling a void to serve their athletic community, the duo opened

  PROJECT

  The subject site resides within South Gate Park, encompassing approximately 96.8 acres
of open space, making it the largest park within city limits. The soccer facility occupies roughly
299,650 square feet of the park's open area, while the clubhouse spans approximately 8,500 square
feet. The proposed beer and wine service will be confined to a designated portion of the existing
clubhouse building. The licensed area for beer and wine consumption will encompass 3,610.58
square feet, inclusive of the lounge, restaurant dining area, party room, diner/cafeteria, kitchen,
and outdoor patio space. All alcohol storage will be housed within or behind the counter area.

  The current soccer facility resides within South Gate Park, comprised of various parcels
owned by the City of South Gate. Consequently, the representatives of the soccer facility are
presently operating under a Ground Lease Agreement with the City, which received prior
approval from the City Council in 2009. Established in 2019, the soccer facility has operated in
accordance with the terms of the Ground Lease Agreement. This agreement would be amended
to accommodate the proposed Conditional Use Permit.

  The Applicant and its principals founded Sofive Soccer Center in South Gate in 2010. The
center has flourished, facilitating adult and youth leagues, tournaments, pickup games, and field
rentals. With an investment exceeding $9 million in its development and enhancement, the site
now welcomes over 250,000 visitors annually. The Center offers numerous advantages to its
patrons and the City of South Gate, as detailed below.
